title: Deploy apps publishes a frontend that needs a newer backend than production runs (CSRF cookie rename)
author: maya
body:

title: Add a person-only local landing route: review and land an agent's change from the CLI
author: maya
body:
First item after the Monday preview (CEO ruling 2026-10-17: the preview claims "durable agent coding on your own subscription; you review the diff and land it yourself").

Today a CLI user cannot review or land an agent's change through Smithers on an ordinary project (bug bash, #4232 comment https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/issues/4232#issuecomment-6245002781):

- compare-and-swap of the target main (refuse if main moved).

title: Uncaptured flow bodies cannot resume after a host restart: plan_changed on the README and quickstart pattern
author: maya
body:
A flow whose body or continuation is an uncaptured function, registered with `Interpreter.layer` (the default `process-local` callback policy) on a durable host, cannot resume after its host restarts. The rebuilt plan carries new `sha256-source-ephemeral/v4` digests, so the recorded-plan check from #3906 refuses the run with `plan_changed` ("start a new execution"). The run is stranded.

This is the pattern every `@smthrs/flows` example teaches: the README's "A flow that survives a restart", `docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/guides/stand-up-a-node-runtime.md` and `docs/guides/change-a-flow-and-keep-the-work.md` all pass a plain arrow `body` (and `bindPlanned` continuation) to `Interpreter.layer` under `NodeRuntime.layerHost`.

Related to #4212 (typed catch filter identity in the TODO plan). This is the broader case: no catch, no schema filter; the flow body alone is enough.

title: New issue on a GitHub-backed repo shows a CLI usage sentence instead of the form
author: maya
body:
Found by the Product Manager's app walk for the 2026-10-17 bug bash (screenshot B39, `codeplanesmithers/canary-sandbox`, a GitHub-backed repository on smithers.sh).

Steps
1. Sign in to https://smithers.sh as a GitHub user and open a GitHub-backed repository.
2. Start a new issue from the app ("Open a GitHub issue", flow `issue.new`, `apps/app/src/mainview/flows/entries/subjects.ts:109`).

Expected
The issue form opens, and submitting it creates the GitHub issue (or the form says what is missing in plain words).

title: flow plan hides why a flow body failed to load, even with --verbose
author: maya
body:
## Symptom

When a flow module fails to import, `smthrs flow plan <name>` and the discovery warning report only a generic sentence. `--verbose` adds nothing:

```text
WARN discovered flow is not runnable on this host { code: 'body_unavailable', reason: 'the body of flow "w" could not be loaded from "…/.smithers/flows/w/flow.ts"' }
code: InvalidInput
message: "invalid_input issue=Cannot load flow w: the body of flow \"w\" could not be loaded from \"…/.smithers/flows/w/flow.ts\""
```

The real cause is dropped. On the published rc.12 it was `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package '@smthrs/registry' imported from …/flows/w/.smithers-<digest>.mjs` (the MDX prompt's JSX runtime). Because the CLI hid it, the plue#836 spike and the #4231 bug bash both diagnosed `@smthrs/agent` from a direct `node` import, which is the wrong package.

## Reproduce on main (556158785a)

Run the CLI from a main checkout in an empty directory outside the repository:

```sh

smthrs init
```

Actual: only the generic "could not be loaded" sentence, with or without `--verbose`.

title: Egress relay delays every streamed response event until the next upstream read
author: maya
body:
## Observed behavior

`packages/backend/egressrelay` delays streamed responses from every host bound to an egress secret.

1. **Masking holdback.** `maskingBody.Read` masks only up to `len(pending) - (longest-1)` and keeps the last `longest-1` bytes of every upstream read until the next read or EOF (`relay.go`, `maskingBody.Read`). An SSE event that ends a read reaches the guest one inter-event gap late. The last event of a stream arrives only at upstream EOF. A response shorter than `longest-1` bytes is held whole until EOF.
2. **Plain-http path never flushes.** `Relay.ServeHTTP` copies a `Config.Local` response with `io.Copy(w, response.Body)` and no `Flush`, so the `net/http` write buffer batches events until it fills or the handler returns. This path serves plain-http local destinations, such as the Mac self-host backend at `127.0.0.1`/`localhost` (`apps/backend/isolation.go`).

Hosted Chat binds the model credential to the model origin (plue `apps/backend/internal/composition/chat.go`), and the worker routes credentialed guest requests to this relay (plue `internal/microsandbox/worker/egress_secrets.go`). The workspace provider pool binds its key the same way. Every hosted model stream goes through `maskingBody`.

## Evidence (main `68f1d8946ed3`, 2026-10-17)

Go tests added in the package through `go test -overlay` (no source change). Upstream writes one ~110-byte SSE event, flushes, and sleeps for the gap. The bound values are the test fixtures; no real secret is invol

title: S.NodeModule.Bin resolves at plan time, before the Install target it depends on runs
author: maya
body:
`S.NodeModule.Bin("<tool>")` resolves `node_modules/.bin/<tool>` when the target is planned, before any of the target's dependencies run. On a fresh checkout the Install target that would create `node_modules` is in the same plan, so planning refuses every such target:

```
//.smithers/effect:check  failed  0ms  node_modules binary not found: node_modules/.bin/tsc (from S.NodeModule.Bin("tsc"))
```

with `data: [install, ...]` declared, where `install` is the workspace's `S.Install` target. The same command passes once `node_modules` exists, so the first run on any fresh clone (a CI checkout, a mounted overlay from #4217) fails and the second succeeds.

Proposed fix: when a `NodeModule.Bin` reference is missing at plan time and the target depends on an Install target, defer resolution (and its executable identity) to execution, after the dependency settles; keep refusing when no dependency could provide it. Workaround in use: `bin: S.PackageManager.bin, args: ["exec", "<tool>", ...]`.

title: WORKSPACE.ts: a repository that builds nothing must still declare a toolchain
author: maya
body:
**Repro (1.0.0-rc.12).** A docs/ops repository (Markdown vault plus `.smithers/flows/`) declares `S.Workspace("x", { repository, cache, discovery })`. `smthrs targets //...` fails: `Workspace requires the Node runtime/packageManager/nodeModules set, an environment, or toolchains`. Declaring only `runtime: S.Runtime.Node(...)` fails with `runtime, packageManager, and nodeModules must be declared together`, so the repo must add a `package.json` and name a lockfile it will never have.

**Proposed fix.** Allow a workspace with no toolchain when it declares no build targets that need one (fail at the target that needs it, not at workspace load), or provide `S.Toolchain.None`.

title: The packaged native filesystem helper is not executable on macOS arm64
author: smithers-agent
body:
Severity: major. Lane bb-effeck-example. macOS arm64, Node v26.11.1, smthrs 1.0.0-rc.12.

Steps: install `npm install -g smthrs@next` into a clean prefix. Download the published @smthrs/platform-node@1.0.0-rc.12 dist tarball; run `tar -tvf platform-node.tgz | rg darwin-arm64/smithers-jj-export`. Use that installed native helper as SMITHERS_WORKSPACE_JJ_EXPORT_BINARY with source-main CLI when following the approved #4231 workaround.

Expected: [project/state docs](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/blob/main/packages/smithers/docs/concepts/project-and-state.md) document the absolute helper override. The packaged native executable should execute.

Actual archive entry: `-rw-r--r-- 0 0 0 13505216 Oct 26 1985 package/bin/darwin-arm64/smithers-jj-export`. Planning exits 1: `descriptor-relative filesystem isolation failed closed: AtomicHelperError: smithers-jj-export is unusable at SMITHERS_WORKSPACE_JJ_EXPORT_BINARY=...`. `chmod u+x` allows the same source-main flow to plan and complete (run-2 in effeck-example).

Diagnosis: published @smthrs/platform-node/bin/darwin-arm64/smithers-jj-export has mode 0644. Inspect native staging/pack file modes and retain executable mode before pack; cover packed archive extraction through process spawn. This is a release artifact issue, not a proposed permission bypass. No helper or isolation checks weakened.

title: CLI help: `smthrs runs --help` hides signal/logs/resume, and `<group> <sub> --help` prints top-level help
author: maya
body:
**Repro (1.0.0-rc.12, inside a project).**
- `smthrs runs --help` lists only `list` and `show`, but `runs signal`, `runs logs`, `runs resume`, `runs output` all work.
- `smthrs runs list --help`, `smthrs memory set --help`, `smthrs memory notes --help` print the top-level product help (agent, branch, todo, ...), exit 0.
- `smthrs flow start --help` works. Outside a project, `smthrs flow run --help` prints top-level help, and `smthrs approvals approve --schema` says "not a command".

**Proposed fix.** Generate group and subcommand help from the one command manifest the dispatcher uses, with a drift test that every dispatchable verb appears in its group's help and that `<group> <sub> --help` never falls through to top-level help.

title: Evaluate a compatible version range for the effect peer instead of an exact pin
author: maya
body:
Smithers publishes `effect` as an exact peer (rc.12: `4.0.4`). Any application that pins a different Effect patch cannot install the CLI or authoring packages in its own workspace. `npm install --save-dev @smthrs/cli@next @smthrs/targets@next` in a `create-effeck` app (which pins `effect@4.0.5` exactly) fails with `ERESOLVE ... peer effect@"4.0.4" from @smthrs/cli@1.0.0-rc.12` (see #4002, bug bash 2026-10-17).

rc.13 moves Smithers to exactly `effect@4.0.5` (with matching `@effect/*`) as a stopgap approved by the CEO. That only moves the collision to the next patch: every Effect app is forced onto whatever exact patch Smithers last released.

1. A compatible range (for example `>=4.0.5 <4.1.0` or `^4.0.5`) for the `effect` and `@effect/*` peers of the published packages, and what breaks across patches (schema identity, `Context` tags, runtime identity checks such as `declaration_dependency_mismatch`).

title: Edge returns HTML 403 for some issue bodies, and smthrs reports it as a login problem
author: maya
body:
### Summary

Smithers Cloud's edge refuses some legitimate issue bodies with an HTML 403 before the request reaches the backend, and `smthrs` reports that 403 as an authorization problem.

### 1. Content-based 403 at the edge

`POST https://api.jjhub.tech/api/repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues` with this JSON body field (title "probe") is refused:

````
Expected: `callerOfLong(): Effect<number, Gone, Needed>`, per docs/NOTES.md ("A caller sees the contract, not the body"; the `contracts` case lists "a contract wider than the body").
Actual: `Effect<number, never, never>`. No EK2002 fires when such a call sits under an `R = never` contract.
````

Evidence, from unauthenticated curl requests (so no auth involved and nothing created):
- A harmless body (`"body":"x"`) gets `404` `application/json` from the backend (`repository not found` for a private repo), with `via: 1.1 google` and an `x-request-id`.
- The paragraph above gets `403` `text/html` (134 bytes: `<!doctype html>...<title>403</title>403 Forbidden`), with no `via` header and no `x-request-id`, so the backend never saw it. title: Agent roles: unattended Explainer seat runs on the Kimi Code subscription (U4)
author: maya
body:
## Summary
The seeded Explainer seat defaults to the Kimi Code subscription model `kimi-for-coding/k3` through `opencode-kimi`. The Explainer runs unattended inside flows, and Kimi Code subscriptions are "for personal interactive use only". Unattended invocations must use the Moonshot API.

## Evidence (main f53d5abfd8a4)
- `packages/rpc/src/AgentRoles.ts:144`: Explainer `model: { provider: "kimi-for-coding", id: "kimi-for-coding/k3" }`, `harness: "opencode-kimi"`.
- `AgentRoles.ts:180`: the UI seat uses the same subscription model.

## Repro
```sh
grep -n 'kimi-for-coding/k3' packages/rpc/src/AgentRoles.ts
```

## Expected
- Seeded unattended seats (Explainer, and UI when a flow invokes it) use a `moonshot` API-key provider.
- `kimi-for-coding` remains only for a person's interactive OpenCode session.

## Why
Kimi Code community guidelines: "Kimi Code subscriptions are for personal interactive use only." Kimi Model Use Agreement (2026-08-31) §4.6(e) forbids "automated scripts… to achieve automated or bulk use." CEO ruling 2026-10-17 (mesh compliance default).

title: Provider pool: subscription usage limit rotates to the next account (U2)
author: maya
body:
## Summary
On a usage limit, `/provider-pool` records the limit and retries the request on the next connected account, up to 8 attempts. For subscription connections (ChatGPT/Codex sign-ins) that is account rotation to bypass usage limits. Failover must stay for API keys only; a subscription limit must reach the caller as a 429 with the reset time.

## Evidence (main f53d5abfd8a4)
- `packages/backend/internal/routes/provider_pool.go:26-36`: "on a usage limit or a refused credential records it and tries the next account before anything reaches the caller."
- `provider_pool.go:381` `modelPoolMaxAttempts = 8`; loop at `:413`.
- Nothing limits a user to one active subscription connection per provider.

## Repro
Connect two Codex sign-ins for one user, make the fake provider answer the first with a usage-limit error, and POST `/provider-pool/chatgpt/codex/responses`: the request succeeds on the second account. `TestProviderPool_RotatesPastALimitedAccountBeforeAnyByteReachesTheCaller` (`packages/backend/internal/routes/provider_pool_test.go:181`) asserts exactly this:


- At most one active subscription connection per user and provider.

- API-key connections keep failover.

title: Provider pool: owner swap bills members' runs to the owner's ChatGPT subscription (U1)
author: maya
body:
## Summary
On a single-owner (self-host) install, `WithProviderPoolOwner` swaps every caller's user id for the install owner's before the pool resolves a connection. A member's coding run is then billed to the owner's ChatGPT subscription. Subscriptions must serve only their account holder; only API-key connections may serve an install's authorized users.

## Evidence (main f53d5abfd8a4)

title: CLI reference names SMITHERS_TELEGRAM_API_BASE_URL and SMITHERS_LINEAR_API_BASE_URL, which nothing reads
author: maya
body:
The CLI reference says an integration entry may use the endpoint named by `SMITHERS_LINEAR_API_BASE_URL` or `SMITHERS_TELEGRAM_API_BASE_URL`. No code reads either variable. `smthrs integrations` accepts only the `github` provider, because #3389 deferred the Linear and Telegram adapters. That issue's acceptance criteria required "docs ... agree", and this paragraph was missed.

## Where

`packages/smithers/docs/reference/cli/README.md`, lines 259–264 at `main@origin` f53d5abf:

> ... and only its provider's public API origin plus the one named by `SMITHERS_GITHUB_API_BASE_URL`, `SMITHERS_LINEAR_API_BASE_URL`, or `SMITHERS_TELEGRAM_API_BASE_URL`.

The code says otherwise. `packages/smithers/src/operator/Integrations.ts:30` has `const provider = z.enum(["github"])`, and the `authority` table holds only `github`. `rg SMITHERS_TELEGRAM_API_BASE_URL` and `rg SMITHERS_LINEAR_API_BASE_URL` find only this README line.

## Repro (smthrs 1.0.0-rc.12)

```sh
d=$(mktemp -d) && mkdir "$d/.smithers"
echo '{"version":1,"integrations":[{"id":"tg","provider":"telegram"}]}' > "$d/.smithers/integrations.json"
smthrs integrations list --root "$d"
# code: operator_failed
# message: "Invalid integrations configuration: integrations.0.provider is invalid"   (exit 1)
```

A reader of the reference page expects a Telegram integration to be configurable. We hit this on 2026-10-17 while setting up Telegram access for the ops org, and had to read the source to learn that Smithers has no Telegram support.

title: Push to a new org repo prints 'remote: error: cannot run : No such file or directory'
author: maya
body:

title: CLI: a login with SMITHERS_AUTH_FILE overwrites the default login's keychain token
author: maya
body:
## What happened

A second `smthrs login` that sets `SMITHERS_AUTH_FILE` to a separate file replaced the default login's token. Afterwards the default record (`~/.config/smithers/auth.json`) signed in as the second user, and the first user's token was gone from the machine. On a shared Mac this silently moved automation from a narrow bot token to a person's broader token.

## Repro (smthrs 1.0.0-rc.12, macOS)

1. Sign in as user A in the default record: `smthrs login https://api.jjhub.tech`. `SMITHERS_API_ORIGIN=https://api.jjhub.tech smthrs auth status` shows A.
2. Sign in as user B into another file: `SMITHERS_AUTH_FILE=/tmp/b-auth.json SMITHERS_API_ORIGIN=https://api.jjhub.tech smthrs login https://api.jjhub.tech`.
3. Run `SMITHERS_API_ORIGIN=https://api.jjhub.tech smthrs auth status` again. It shows B.
4. `security find-generic-password -s smithers-cli -a jjhub.tech` shows one item, modified at step 2.

Expected: `SMITHERS_AUTH_FILE` isolates the whole credential, so the default record still resolves to A.

## Cause

- The keychain item is keyed only by service and host: `add-generic-password -U -s smithers-cli -a <host>` (`packages/smithers/src/internal/backend/Session.ts:403`, reads at `:405-411`).
- `resolve()` reads that keychain item for any record bound to the origin, before the record's own token (`Session.ts:472-480`). Every auth file for one host therefore shares one keychain item, and `-U` overwrites it.

## Suggested fix

- Key the keychain item by the auth rec

title: Install flow recreates node_modules on every run for Effect's pnpm workspace
author: maya
body:
In the Effect overlay (#4217) every command that reaches the Install target prints `Recreating <root>/node_modules` and spends 15 to 25 seconds relinking 1,069 packages, even when nothing changed. The Install flow runs `pnpm fetch --frozen-lockfile` and then `pnpm install --offline`; the first step reports the recreate. Effect's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` sets `enableGlobalVirtualStore: false` and `verifyDepsBeforeRun: error`, so the likely cause is a settings mismatch between the two steps that makes pnpm discard the modules directory.

Expected: an unchanged lockfile and workspace file leave `node_modules` in place, and the Install target settles in about a second.

title: smthrs install finds the Install target only in the root package
author: maya
body:
`smthrs install` selects the Install target only from the root package (`packagePath === ""`) and fails with `the root PACKAGE.ts declares no Install target` otherwise. An overlay mounted onto an upstream repository (#4217) holds only `.smithers/`, so it declares its Install target in a `.smithers/<name>/PACKAGE.ts` and cannot satisfy the verb. Targets that depend on the Install target still install through the graph; only the verb is unusable.

Proposed fix: when the root package declares no Install target, use the workspace's single Install target, and keep refusing when there are several.

title: pnpm 11 exec fails under the confined sandbox: store probe writes <root>/_tmp_*
author: maya
body:
Under the confined sandbox, pnpm 11's `pnpm exec` (and so `S.Typecheck`, `S.Vitest`, and every rule that renders `PackageManager.exec`) fails before the tool starts:

```
[ERROR] EPERM: operation not permitted, open '<workspace>/_tmp_57798_633f6b0a3f042e5187814ead58ec3682'
sandbox: _tmp_… is outside the declared read set
```

pnpm resolves its store location at startup. With no store directory configured it calls `storePathRelativeToHome`, which `touch`es `<lockfileDir>/_tmp_<pid>_<hash>` to probe the filesystem and does not catch EPERM. `--config.verify-deps-before-run=false` and `manage-package-manager-versions=false` do not avoid it. Setting `pnpm_config_store_dir` does (verified with `sandbox-exec` and a profile that denies `<root>/_tmp_*`).

Proposed fix: give every pnpm tool run the store directory the Install flow already passes as `--store-dir` (`<root>/.flows/store/pnpm`), through `pnpm_config_store_dir`, so exec never probes the workspace root. The Smithers repository does not see this because its workspace declares `default: S.Sandbox.None()`.

Found while mounting the Effect overlay (#4217); pnpm 11.20.0, macOS seatbelt.

title: Confined Shell.Test cannot list directories that hold its declared inputs
author: maya
body:
A confined `Shell.Test` on macOS (the default seatbelt sandbox) cannot list the directories that hold its declared inputs, so a tool that discovers files by walking a directory finds nothing.

Reproduction (Effect overlay, #4217): with `data: [S.glob("//packages/effect/src/**/*.ts"), ...]` declared,

```ts
S.Shell.Test({ bin: S.NodeModule.Bin("tsc"), args: ["-p", "packages/effect/tsconfig.json", "--noEmit", ...], data })
```

fails with `error TS18003: No inputs were found in config file '.../packages/effect/tsconfig.json'. Specified 'include' paths were '["src"]'`. The same command passes with `sandbox: "none"`. tsc's `include`, Vitest's `include`, and oxlint's path argument all list directories.

`ProcessSandbox` grants `file-read*` on each declared file and, in strict mode, only `file-read-metadata` on their ancestors, so `readdir(packages/effect/src)` is denied.

Proposed fix: grant directory listing (`file-read-data` on the directory literal, not its subtree) for every directory between a declared glob's literal prefix and the files it matched. A listing reveals names, not contents, and only names under a prefix the target already declared.

title: pnpm's verify-deps flag is prepended to non-pnpm tools invoked with run
author: maya
body:
`PackagePlanner` prepends `--config.verifyDepsBeforeRun=false` to any planned argv whose second token is `exec` or `run` when the workspace manager is pnpm. It never checks that the first token is pnpm, so a workspace tool invoked as `run` receives pnpm's flag:

```ts
S.Shell.Test({ bin: S.NodeModule.Bin("vitest"), args: ["run", "--project", "effect"] })
```

runs `node_modules/.bin/vitest --config.verifyDepsBeforeRun=false run --project effect`, and Vitest crashes parsing `--config.verifyDepsBeforeRun` (`TypeError: Cannot create property ...` in its cac parser).

Fix: prepend the flag only when argv[0] is the pnpm executable. Regression test in `packages/smithers/build/build-cli/test/WorkspaceToolchainExecution.test.ts` ("package-manager flags").

Found while mounting the Effect overlay (#4217).

title: J5: a TODO whose prefix moves needs the native rebase while its run blocks in stack.propose
author: maya
body:
J5 row 15b ("Repository copy executes D2") still fails about one run in three on a Linux VM. TODO C's candidate is accepted, then TODO A's verified head moves C's prefix. Since a18b6c3bc9, `stack.propose` waits (202) for the stack's rebase of C's own candidate instead of refusing it. That fixes the plain-rebase case: the stack rebases within a second and the delivery re-captures and proposes (`reserved_candidate_rebased`, spec 10.4.1).

In the failing runs the rebase needs the branch daemon's native rewrite (`executeNativeRebase` in `branch_rebase_execution.go`). The item stays `integrating` / `rebase_pending` for the whole 3-minute window. My reading, not yet proven by a trace: the daemon refuses the native rewrite as `busy` because a writer session on C's machine is still open, and that session is C's TODO run, which is blocked inside the `stack.propose` call. That is a circular wait. After 180 s the native helper returns `workspace_busy`, the run ends as a `wait` outage, and the TODO is retried, which is too late for the row.

Spec 10.4.1 describes the intended shape: after `stack.propose` the run waits for a stack event ("clean rebase onto a new tip → candidate → check → stack.propose"). The stack never signals the run when it rebases (no `rebased` signal exists), so the run cannot park, release its session and resume. Options: (a) refuse `stack.propose` quickly while a native rebase is blocked on this run's own session, and have the delivery park on a durable wait the st

title: GitHub sync can deadlock with stack requests on mythical_stacks and repositories (J7 HTTP 500)
author: maya
body:
`POST /api/github/sync` failed with HTTP 500 `deadlock detected (SQLSTATE 40P01)` in the J7 rehearsal (row "16 main moves cleanly"), on a Linux VM running 12 rehearsals at once. The same row passed in an earlier run on the same build, so it is intermittent and load-dependent.

PostgreSQL's report: three transactions in a cycle. Two run `RequestMythicalStack` (`UPDATE mythical_stacks SET requested_generation = requested_generation + 1 ... WHERE repository_id = $1`, `packages/backend/internal/db/mythical_ext.go`), one runs `SELECT generation FROM mythical_stacks WHERE repository_id=$1 FOR UPDATE`. One of the UPDATEs waits while taking the foreign-key `FOR KEY SHARE` lock on the `repositories` row, so at least one transaction locks `repositories` (or a row whose FK check takes it) before `mythical_stacks`, and another in the opposite order.

```
Process 814901 waits for ShareLock on transaction 305816; blocked by process 814905.
Process 814905 waits for ShareLock on transaction 305817; blocked by process 814896.
Process 814896 waits for AccessExclusiveLock on tuple (0,13) of relation mythical_stacks; blocked by process 814901.
814901, 814905: UPDATE mythical_stacks SET requested_generation = requested_generation + 1 ... WHERE repository_id = $1
814896: SELECT generation FROM mythical_stacks WHERE repository_id=$1 FOR UPDATE
CONTEXT (814905): while locking tuple (0,2) in relation "repositories"
  SELECT 1 FROM ONLY "public"."repositories" x WHERE "id" = $1 FOR KEY SHARE OF x
```

title: Typed catch filters have process-local plan identity, so a TODO resumed after a host restart fails plan_changed
author: maya
body:
A typed `Node.catch({ error: SomeSchema, ... })` records `filterIdentity`, which `@smthrs/plan` (`internal/node.ts` `filterIdentity`) builds from every function in the schema AST. Those functions are unannotated, so the identity is `sha256-source-ephemeral/v4`: stable inside one process, different in every new process.

Consequence: the durable interpreter records the plan digest (#3906) and refuses a resume whose rebuilt digest differs (`plan_changed`). The built-in TODO plan contains one typed catch (`coding/request-flow.ts`, `Node.catch({ error: CodingError, ... })`), so a TODO that parks (Needs you, Stop) and is resumed by a **restarted** host fails with "The rebuilt plan differs from the recorded plan". Same-process resumes now pass (every callback is captured in 642f333139).

Reproduction (two processes, same source):

```
cd .smithers/flows
# print each FunctionIdentity digest in Graph.drafts(Graph.build(todo, payload)); run twice
```

Only `...then.flow.then.then.filterIdentity` differs between the two runs; all 33 other callback identities match.

Options: give schema filters a stable identity (for example the schema's canonical JSON identity plus captured identities of declared checks), or let `Node.catch` take a captured filter. `.smithers/flows/test/coding-stable-plan.test.ts` currently excludes `filter` diagnostics with a comment pointing here; remove that exclusion when fixed.

title: Docker push executor fixture inherits a missing Windows shell refusal
author: maya
body: Hosted Windows job117330648732 has24 DockerPushExecution.test failures reporting dependency //:image did not succeed.
